tossups.text: Supalla and Newport found that "hold manners" could distinguish similar noun-verb pairs in this language. The term "chereme" was coined while William Stokoe was studying this language. Two pluses represent repetition in glosses of this language, in which comparisons are made using contrastive structure. The "Black" variant of this language often uses a lower space for adverbs. The spread of this language contributed to the decline of a similar language in Chilmark, a town on Martha's Vineyard. It's not English, but this language is an official language of Washington D.C.'s Gallaudet University. For 10 points, facial expressions and fingerspelling are important features of what native language of most deaf people in the United States?

Philosophy: Excommunication, In About An Hour His skepticism about the authorship of the Pentateuch and the existence of God resulted in his excommunication from his synagogue. Making a living as a lensmaker, he was able to write down his thoughts in Tractatus Theologico-Politicus. For 15 points-name this Dutch rationalist philosopher who discussed his pantheistic beliefs in the 1677 treatise Ethics.

Labor camps in this nation were compared to an "archipelago" in one book. One leader of this nation implemented a policy of "dekulakization," in which wealthy peasants were declared "class enemies." That policy was part of this nation's First Five-Year Plan, which emphasized "Socialism in One Country." This country created a secret police force called the NKVD, which later evolved into the KGB. For 10 points, name this communist nation that was once led by Josef Stalin.

He made the career of Johann Gottlieb Fichte by publishing the latter's Attempt at a Critique of All Revelation. In 1770, he claimed that the works of David Hume "awoke [him] from [his] dogmatic slumber." He went on to explain "the starry heavens above...and the moral law within..." in such works as The Metaphysics of Morals. For 10 points-name this German transcendentalist who posited the categorical imperative in Critique of Judgment and Critique of Pure Reason.

After one of these conflicts, the title of princeps was taken by Godfrey of Bouillon ["BOOL-yaan"]. Frederick Barbarossa drowned in the Saleph River during the third of these conflicts. Crowds chanted "deus vult" at Pope Urban II in support of one of these conflicts, the third of which saw Richard the Lionheart make peace with Saladin. The first of these conflicts in 1099 ended with the conquest of Jerusalem. For 10 points, name these medieval Catholic military expeditions attempting to retake the Holy Land.

A planned highway across this region called BR-230 is largely unpaved between Altamira and Benjamin Constant. Most of the state of Mato Grosso is south of this region; Mato Grosso also includes some of the Pantanal wetlands. Contrary to popular belief, the red-eyed tree frog is not native to this region, but piranhas and anacondas are. Dust from the Sahara Desert blows across the Atlantic Ocean to fertilize, for 10 points, what massive tropical ecosystem around the longest river in South America?

This author wrote about Eben Cabot, who goes to jail with his father's wife Abbie Putnam after she kills their baby in Desire Under the Elms. In another work by this author, the daughter of a steel tycoon, Mildred Douglas, calls the coal stoker Yank a "dirty beast." This man set another one of his plays in Harry Hope's Saloon, where the "Great Salesman" Hickey tells his friends to give up on their pipe dreams. This author of The Hairy Ape wrote about the mother of the Tyrone family, Mary, who suffers from morphine addiction. For 10 points, name this American playwright of The Iceman Cometh and A Long Day's Journey into Night.

In his Determinatio, John of Paris promoted a doctrine named after this thing which holds that this substance is incarnated by God. In the Coptic Church, a form of this thing called qurban often features an image of a cross surrounded by twelve dots.This thing is placed on top of artoklasia tables at the very end of some Orthros rituals. During the Proskomedia, a large seal consisting of the letters "IC, XC, and NIKA" is used to sanctify this substance. Antidoron is a form of this thing which is made from discarded components of the prosphora. When it is used for rituals, this thing is carried in the diskos. In the West, the ciborium and the smaller paten is used to hold it. According to Ulrich Zwingli's position at the Marburg colloquy, it is said to become flesh. Consumed alongside grape juice or wine is, for 10 points, what substance that turns into the body of Christ during Eucharist?

In the late 1960s and early 1970s, an activist group involving these people occupied Mount Rushmore and Alcatraz. Tahlequah, Oklahoma, was a destination for these people after their forced relocation by the Treaty of New Echota. A league of these people named the Iroquois fought in the Seven Years' War. The Trail of Tears relocated, for 10 points, what people who lived in the New World before European colonization?

A gas station attendant tells this family about a scheme to paint pumps yellow. A member of this family hands out candy to children to atone for being too cheap to hire a doctor for his dead wife. Despite working as strikebreakers to pick peaches, a member of this family avenges the death of the labor organizer and preacher Jim Casey. In order to save a starving man, a member of this family named Rose of Shannon breastfeeds him. For 10 points, Tom is a member of what family that migrates to California in John Steinbeck's The Grapes of Wrath?

A woman nicknamed the "Red Virgin" of a neighbourhood in this city is credited with the first use of the anarchist black flag. Thousands of prisoners were killed in this city during the September Massacres. The closing of this city's national workshops led to the June Days uprising. The widening of streets in this city by Baron Haussmann ("ohs-MAHN") decreased the efficacy of barricades. Political factions in this city included The Mountain. A radical commune in this city was created after an 1871 defeat to Prussia. The Marquis of Launay was killed in an attack on a prison in this city on July 14, 1789. For 10 points, name this city where the storming of the Bastille began the French Revolution.

This author wrote a short story in which a woman screams after finding a bull-whip in her wash-basin. In that story, Delia feels a "surge of pity" while sitting under a Chinaberry tree as her abusive husband Sykes dies from a snakebite. This author studied the life of the "Voodoo Queen" Marie Laveau while collecting black folk tales for an anthropological study discussed in her autobiography Dust Tracks on a Road. In another novel by this author, Leafy abandons her daughter who later runs off with the mayor of Eatonville, Jody Starks. That woman is later acquitted for shooting her rabies-infected husband Tea Cake during a hurricane. For 10 points, name this author of Their Eyes Were Watching God.

The original Legoland park can be found in this country's city of Billund. This country's mainland is part of the Jutland Peninsula. This country's capital is home to the Tivoli Gardens and lies across the Oresund Strait from Malmo, Sweden. A Hans Christian Andersen story inspired the Little Mermaid Statue in the capital of this Scandinavian country. For 10 points, name this country north of Germany, whose capital is Copenhagen.

Paul Gauguin and this other painter briefly lived together in Arles in 1888, and Gauguin painted a portrait of this man he called "the Painter of Sunflowers." This Dutch artist's work includes The Potato Eaters and a Self-Portrait with Straw Hat. Plagued by bouts of mental illness, this artist is also known for cutting off his own ear and giving it to Gauguin. For 10 points, name this artist perhaps best known for his painting The Starry Night.

Description acceptable. The Diary of Joseph Naples recounts the author's time in this profession, which enriched Jack Hartnett and Ben Crouch before rumors about it ruined their fortunes. A prominent practitioner of this profession had his skeleton articulated and displayed at Edinburgh Medical School after his hanging. Levi Parmley, the inventor of dental floss, may have done extensive business with a mysterious member of this profession known as Butler, who followed Wellington's armies in the Peninsular War. A crackdown on this profession ensued after the murder of 16 people in Scotland by two of its members, William Burke and William Hare. Articles in the Terrific Register likely inspired Charles Dickens to portray this profession with the character of Jerry Cruncher in A Tale of Two Cities. For 10 points, name this profession that supplied scientific researchers like Andreas Vesalius, whose members often lurked around cemeteries.
acceptableAnswers: accept descriptive answers relating to people who sold corpses

tossups.text: Kai Erikson's Everything in Its Path documented the aftermath of an impoundment dam flood in this state, which killed 125 people along Buffalo Creek. During the 1912 Paint Creek-Cabin Creek strike in this state, Mother Jones was kept under house arrest. The Logan Defenders opposed an uprising of laborers who wanted to unionize in its Battle of Blair Mountain. The southern part of this state includes much of the Winding Gulf Coalfields. After the 2010 Upper Big Branch Mine disaster in this state, former Massey Energy CEO Don Blankenship was jailed. An older event in this present-day state ended after Robert E. Lee captured its leader in the engine house of an arsenal. For 10 points, in what present-day state did John Brown's raid on Harpers Ferry occur?

Possible causes of these events include photo-disintegration, pair instability, and electron capture, each of which leads to core collapse. White dwarfs that grow larger than the Chandrasekhar limit can undergo the Type Ia [one A] variety of this event. The Crab Nebula was formed by one of these events in 1054 CE, leading some people to believe a new star had been born. For 10 points, name these incredibly powerful explosions of stars.

Granules containing excessive amounts of this element in certain cells are known as Pappenheimer bodies and this element is chelated by siderophores. A gamma ray emitting isotope of this element with a molecular weight of 57 was used to verify the predictions of general relativity by Pound and Rebka. This element can be dumped into the ocean to induce algal blooms. This element is found between two cyclopentadiene ligands in the first "sandwich" metallocene complex ever synthesized. This element is generally purified from ores like magnetite and hematite. A deficiency of this element can lead to anemia. For 10 points, name this element found in hemoglobin, with symbol Fe.

A city on this body of water contains a "Little Venice" neighborhood on its Pearl Islands. Two countries on this body of water dispute the Hawar Islands. The King Fahd Causeway leads to an island nation in this body of water, which contains the World and Palm Jumeirah artificial islands. High casualties amongst Indian migrant workers have occurred while constructing 2022 FIFA World Cup stadiums along this body of water. Qeshm is a large island near the Strait of Hormuz, which separates this body of water from the Gulf of Oman and the Indian Ocean. For 10 points, name this gulf located between the Arabian Peninsula and Iran.
acceptableAnswers: accept just Arabian after “ gulf” and before “Arabian”

tossups.text: The Keppler circle promoted this politician by drafting the Industrial petition. This politician announced his beliefs in a twenty-five-point program that would serve as his party's platform. This politician forced the resignation of Anton Drexler and enacted the Enabling Act after the arrest of Marinus van der Lubbe. This man was arrested along with Erich Ludendorff after leading the Beer Hall Putsch. This politician ordered the execution of Ernst Röhm in the Night of the Long Knives. In 1933, Paul von Hindenburg appointed this politician chancellor. For 10 points, name this politician who later led Germany during the Second World War.

parts.text: Name this factor. A branch of economics named after this concept examines how supply and demand for it affect things like wages and income.
The increase in productivity as a result of a division of labor was discussed by this classical economist in his Wealth of Nations.
In this treatise that criticizes conspicuous consumption, Thorstein Veblen argues that the division of labor resulted in lower classes being the only ones in productive occupations.
acceptableAnswers: The Theory of the Leisure Class

bonuses.leadin: The four factors of production include land, capital, entrepreneurship and this concept, whose division is the subject of a work by Emile Durkheim. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this mustached German philosopher whose ideas include the unrestricted, superhuman übermensch. He declared that "God is dead" before going insane.
This title prophet of a Nietzsche work, named for a real-world prophet, comes down from the mountains to discsuss "eternal recurrence" and hail the age of the übermensch.

Name or description acceptable. After Nietzsche went mad, this anti-Semitic caretaker edited and controlled his work. This member of a failed Aryan colony in Paraguay compiled rough notes into The Will to Power and promoted Nietzsche to early Nazis.

bonuses.leadin: This philosopher described a madman with a lantern in his The Gay Science, and believed that the post-Christian world of his day was still stuck with "slave morality.". For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this December 7, 1941 surprise attack on the US Pacific fleet. Over 2,400 Americans were killed in this attack in Hawaii.

Crucially for the US fleet, their three ships of this type, including the Enterprise, were out at sea during the attack. The fact that the Japanese did not know where these American ships were contributed to the decision against a third wave.
Over 1,100 men were killed in the sinking of this battleship in Pearl Harbor. A floating memorial over the hull of this ship commemorates those lost during the attack.

bonuses.leadin: Although fuel concerns and improving American counterattacking forced a withdrawal, Admiral Yamamoto later lamented the cancellation of the third wave of this attack. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this curve used to show the opportunity cost of making two goods. It is commonly illustrated using guns and butter.

This activity allows production to exceed the PᐧPᐧF. Tariffs are barriers to this activity, which David Ricardo illustrated the comparative advantage of using the example of English cloth and Portuguese wine.

The British Empire practiced this form of trade, in which resources extracted from colonies and trade barriers were used to maximize exports and minimize imports. Adam Smith opposed this idea, preferring free trade.

bonuses.leadin: Points inside this curve are inefficient, and economic growth causes this curve to move outward. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The South's blocking of voting rights bypassed the fifteenth one of these pieces of legislation, which gave all African-Americans voting rights. The thirteenth of these pieces of legislation banned slavery.
Jim Crow laws forced African-Americans to pay these fees if they wanted to vote, until they were banned by the Twenty-Fourth Amendment.

Poll taxes and grandfather clauses were some of the ways people in the South prevented African-Americans from voting during this period of US history, which ended with the presidency of Rutherford B. Hayes.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about ways the post-Civil War South prevented African-Americans from voting, for 10 points each:

parts.text: This province, with capital at Toronto, is also home to Canada's capital city of Ottawa.
Extremists in this predominately French speaking province regularly agitate for secession.
The only officially bilingual province is this Maritime Province east of the state of Maine.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name these Canadian provinces.

parts.text: Name this play in which Karl Moor becomes part of the titular group of outlaws after he is cursed by his father, but willingly surrenders to the law after the death of all his family.
This German wrote The Robbers, as well as the play Wilhelm Tell and the poem Ode to Joy, which was used in a symphony by Beethoven.
Schiller wrote this trilogy of plays about the namesake Thirty Years' War general known for his brutality and served by men such as Ottavio Piccolomini.

bonuses.leadin: In this play, Franz tries to kill his father the Count by locking him in a vault and also tries to steal his brother's love Amalia. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this text that is read on Shavuot. Many scholars interpret the protagonist's choice to sneak in and "uncover the feet" of another character as a sexual euphemism.
Like Ruth on Shavuot, this text is read on Purim, which celebrates freedom from Achaemenid persecution under the vizier Haman after the title character's cousin Mordecai refused to bow down to him.
In the Ketuvim, Ruth and Esther are included among the "Five Megillot" or "Scrolls," short texts of unusual genre, along with Lamentations. Name both of the other two Megillot texts.
acceptableAnswers: accept the alternatives Song of Solomon
and Šīr hašŠīrīm for the first text

bonuses.leadin: This text, thought to be a historical repudiation of the ideology found in Ezra-Nehemiah, is held in esteem by some Jewish converts because its protagonist was a Moabite who became Jewish by marriage. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this country, whose "Upper" and "Lower" regions were unified by one of its pharaohs, Narmer.
Hor-Aha politely named a year the "Year of the Smiting of [this region]" after leading a campaign against it. This region directly south of Egypt was later ruled by the Kingdom of Kush.
acceptableAnswers: the “Year of the Smiting of Nubia

parts.text: Hor-Aha is possibly conflated with Narmer on the prehistoric king list on the Palermo Stone, which is named for the capital of this triangular island in the middle of the Mediterranean Sea.

bonuses.leadin: One ruler of this country, Hor-Aha, died after being carried off during a hunt by a hippo. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this book, whose title character marries his cousin, who had previously been wed to a schoolteacher named Mr. Phillotson.
Jude the Obscure is set in Wessex, a fictional region created this British author. Wessex is also the setting for this author's Tess of the d'Urbervilles.

This other Hardy novel takes its title from Thomas Gray's "Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard." It features a love quadrilateral comprised of Gabriel Oak, William Boldwood, Francis Troy, and Bathsheba Everdene.
acceptableAnswers: The Far from the Madding Crowd

bonuses.leadin: One character in this book kills his siblings and himself, then leaves a note saying, "Done because we are too menny." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these monuments, which are named for the town where they still stand, between the burial mounds of Thyrvé and her husband, King Gorm the Old.
The other Stone was erected by Gorm's son in his memory, and records this man's conversion of Denmark to Christianity. A form of wireless connection was named for him centuries later.

Harald was forced out of Denmark by this man, his son. Ruling Norway as well, this man raided England repeatedly in the first decade of the millennium to avenge the St Brice's Day massacre, eventually seizing the English throne.

bonuses.leadin: The older of these two monuments is inscribed "in memory of Thyrvé, his wife, Denmark's adornment." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this husband of Amalia who takes his stepdaughter home after meeting her in a brothel.
acceptableAnswers: but do not reveal the father of Six Characters in Search of an Author

parts.text: That father appears in this play, which ends with the Director exclaiming that "I've lost a whole day over [the title group]" after a mute boy shoots himself with a revolver.
parts.answer: Six Characters in Search of an Author
acceptableAnswers: Six Characters in Search of an Author
The Six Characters in Search of an Author

parts.text: This Italian playwright wrote Six Characters in Search of an Author.

bonuses.leadin: Description acceptable. This character explains that Sancho Panza and Don Abbondio were able to live forever because "they had the fortune to find a fecundating matrix". For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this activity, often performed as a ritual to the gods in Polynesian cultures. The hula, often performed at luau feasts, is a form of this activity.
The hula is often considered an official dance of this US state in the Pacific Ocean. This archipelagic state has its capital at Honolulu.
The All Blacks are the national rugby team of this Polynesian country. This country is known by its native people as Aotearoa.

bonuses.leadin: One form of this activity, known as the haka, is performed by a team known as the All Blacks. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this white rock, which ancient Greek sculptors often used for their sculptures.
The marble columns of the Parthenon were constructed in this simplest ancient Greek order, which is contrasted with the more decorative Ionic and Corinthian orders.
Controversially, this museum in London still holds Elgin's Marbles, a series of sculptures Lord Elgin removed from the Parthenon.

bonuses.leadin: The exterior of the Parthenon was constructed using this rock. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this man who rose from the governorship of Antioquia to the presidency of his nation, Colombia.

During his tenure, Uribe, with the help of U.S. resources, upped the military campaign against this Marxist guerilla organization, several of whose leaders, including Manuel Marulanda Velez and Mono Jojoy, have recently died or been killed.
Uribe also managed to effect the release by the FARC, after six years of captivity, of this Colombian politician and founder of the Green Oxygen Party.

bonuses.leadin: This man was succeeded by Juan Manuel Santos, who founded the Social Party of National Unity in support of this man. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this ill-fated shipping company that took its name from the company that ran the Titanic.
The Black Star Line was part of this man's Back-to-Africa movement, along with his newspaper Negro World. He claimed to respect the KKK, and W.E.B. Du Bois called him "a lunatic or a traitor."
Marcus Garvey was ultimately deported to this country on charges of mail fraud. Some Rastafarians from this country believe Garvey was a prophet.

bonuses.leadin: This company ran ships such as the Yarmouth and the Antonio Maceo, which was previously owned by the robber baron Henry H. Rogers. For 10 points each:

parts.text: In this type of reaction, a base that has an extra hydroxide ion and an acid with an extra hydrogen ion form a salt and water.
Like an Arrhenius reaction, this doubly-eponymous reaction involves an acid giving a hydrogen ion to the base, but conjugate acids and bases are formed instead.
This is the name given to a special type of Lewis acid catalyst, which is used in asymmetric synthesis reactions. This word also describes a compound that is non-superposable on its mirror image.

bonuses.leadin: Identify the following about acid-base reactions, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Chugaev developed one of these reactions that converts an alcohol to an alkene through a xanthate intermediate. In these reactions, a proton and a leaving group are lost to form a double bond.
The Chugaev elimination uses an iodo derivative of this simplest alkane with formula CH4. This molecule is the primary constituent of natural gas.
Chugaev discovered the Chugaev elimination during his studies of thujene, a member of this class of organic molecules that consist of 5-carbon isoprene subunits.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about Russian chemist Lev Chugaev, for 10 points each.

parts.text: According to some measurements, the rainiest city in the contiguous United States is Forks, located on the Olympic Peninsula west of Puget Sound in this state.

The rainiest place in the United States as a whole is Mt. Waialeale on this Hawaiian island. This is the farthest west of the major Hawaiian islands, and it's the fourth-largest, after the Big Island, Maui, and O'ahu.

Several of the rainiest places in the world, including Cherrapunji, are located in this cloudy northeastern state of India. This state runs east-west between Assam to its north and Bangladesh to its south.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each-name some locations around the world that are famous for their rainfall:

parts.text: This Virginia politician and first Secretary of State defeated incumbent John Adams in the election. This author of the Declaration of Independence later negotiated the Louisiana Purchase with France during his presidency.
John Adams's running mate in the election, Charles Cotesworth, had this last name. Another politician with this last name, Thomas, negotiated a namesake 1795 treaty between the U.S. and Spain.

Samuel Smith, who secured the winning vote for Jefferson in the contingency election, was a representative from this state. During the War of 1812, Smith led this state's militia and the British won the Battle of Bladensburg.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each: answer the following about the American presidential election of 1800.
